full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case are that the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 139 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna for declarations that the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 02.06.1962 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna in Title Suit No. 319 of 1961 and the judgment and decree dated 31.08.1973 passed by the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Khulna in Title Suit No. 244 of 1966 and the order dated 23.12.1970 passed by Assistant Commissioner (Revenue) in Miscellaneous Case No. 180 of 1971 to the fraudulent, forged, collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff contending, inter-alia, that the land of District Settlement Khatian No.82 of mouza Boyarjhap under Police Station Paikgacha District Khulna measuring an area of 9.44 acres belonged to Monmatha and Narendra who settled that land by a registered Kabuliyat dated 22nd Chaitra 1305 B.S. in favour of Ram Krishana Sana and Mohim Sana. That Kabuliyat was executed by Ram Krishana Sana as being the Karta of Joint Family and that was acquired out of the joint family income. Both brothers got possession. Ram Krishna Sana died leaving behind his widow Billa Dasi and one daughter Laxmi Dasi and full brother Mohim Sana. There was a partition amongst the landlords and the suit land fell in the share of Narendra Mitra. Narendra Mitra demanded a fresh Kabuliyat and Mohim Sana and Billa Dasi executed a Kabuliyat dated 06.01.1921 in favour of Narendra Mitre in respect of the suit land. The C.S. Khatian No.82 was recorded in respect of 9.44 acres of land in the name of Billa Dasi and Mohim Sana. Mohim Sana died leaving behind his only son, Ashini who got 4.72 acres of land. Thereafter, Billa Dasi died leaving behind Ashini Sana as reversioner as her husband. This way the entire 9.44 acres of land was devolved upon Ashini who sold 1.64 acres of land in favour of latish and Kalipada. The R.S. Khatian No.4 was recorded in their names. 'thereafter, Ashini transferred 1.64 acres of land in favour of Nilkrishna. After that transfer Ashini died leaving behind his full sister Patty Dasi who died leaving behind the plaintiffs and accordingly, the land measuring an area 6.18 acres left by Ashini devolved upon the plaintiffs who used to pay rent through one Gurupada Sana. Ashini fell ill before the C.S. operation was held and took shelter in the residence of her full sister. During that time the suit land was being looked after by Gurupada in 1991. The plaintiffs wanted to transfer some land and demanded rent receipts and other papers from Gurupada who failed to return back the papers saying that those were188destroyed. Thereafter, the plaintiff No.11 went to the concerned Tashil officer on 25.04.1991 and the Tashilder disclosed that the suit land was recorded in the name of Guru Charan on the basis of an order passed in Mutation Case No.100 of 1970-71 who produced the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 319 of 1961 and Title Suit No. 244 of 1966. The plaintiff alleged those decrees were fraudulent, collusive, illegal, forged. The defendant' being the heirs of Guru Charan got those decree without issuing any summons upon the plaintiffs and hence the suit.
